overview: The Small Business Administration's (SBA) 504 loan program helps small businesses buy buildings, land, and major equipment through loans partly backed by the federal government and made with nonprofit community lenders called certified development companies. Each year, Congress sets a ceiling on how much in 504 loans the SBA can guarantee. Starting in fiscal year 2027, this bill would let the SBA go up to 15 percent above that ceiling if it expects demand to exceed the limit. The SBA would have to notify the small business and appropriations committees in the House and Senate at least 30 days in advance, and could use this authority only once a year. As of October 9, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say the change keeps a popular loan program from running out of lending room late in the year, so small businesses aren't left waiting while Congress acts to raise the cap.
against: Critics say letting the agency exceed a limit Congress set weakens Congress's control over federal loan guarantees and could increase the government's financial exposure if more loans go bad.
